# Progress — open-spyro C-match

**Game code matched: 2,106,332 / 2,106,332 bytes (100.00%)** — generated by `make progress` (`open-spyro progress`).

Headline folds **2,106,332 bytes exact** (verified byte-identical) with **0 bytes partial** — instruction-level credit for parked `.c.wip` attempts that don't yet fully match (`open-spyro partial`). Because partial credit tracks in-progress C, the headline can move *non-monotonically* (an edit or permuter run may lower a partial score while making real progress); the exact figure above never regresses without a real loss of a match.

Status: `matched` = verified byte-identical from C · `wip` = C in progress (may carry partial credit) · `asm` = original assembly (`INCLUDE_ASM`).

Excluded from the percentage: **439 library functions / 63,308 bytes** of stock PSY-Q SDK + libc statically linked into the EXE (tracked for completeness, but not ours to decompile).

Also excluded: **100 hand-written assembly functions / 97,104 bytes** — Insomniac's math/vector/GTE library and the hot render/collision loops, written directly in asm (they use `$at` as a data register or signed `addi`/`add`/`sub`, which the gcc→aspsx toolchain cannot emit). These can never be matched from C, so they are tracked but kept out of the denominator.

Also excluded: **0 un-split overlay blobs / 0 bytes**. These overlays have no seeded function symbols yet — their asm is a few coarse `func_` blocks that are mostly level *data* (geometry/moby tables) disassembled as code, not matchable C. They are kept out of the denominator until the overlay is function/data-split (at which point their real code counts). See the map for where they sit.

Note: each level overlay contains one ~30-40 KB moby-dispatch megafunction (`func_level_N_*`) — genuine code (prologue/epilogue, a giant switch on the moby type byte). These are ordinary unmatched `asm` counted in the denominator; they are simply the largest single match targets remaining (1.31 MB across 35 functions).
